def: The per-function register space (256 bytes PCI-compatible, 4 KiB with PCIe extended space) holding identity, command/status, BARs and capability structures; read by enumeration software, lspci and drivers.
A memory-mapped window in which each PCIe function's 4 KiB configuration space has a fixed address; CPU loads and stores there become configuration read/write requests.

Linux utility that reads PCI configuration space through sysfs and decodes it: one-line inventory, topology tree (-tv), full capability decode (-vv/-vvv) or hex dumps (-x/-xxx/-xxxx). Decoding beyond the 64-byte header needs root.
Linux utility that reads (register name alone) or writes (register=value) individual configuration registers. Reads are safe inspection; writes bypass the driver and are expert-only operations.

Kernel-provided virtual filesystem exposing devices, drivers and their attributes as files, e.g. /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:01:00.0/current_link_speed, /sys/class/nvme/nvme0/state, /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/.

The Linux 'nvme' tool that sends NVMe admin and I/O commands through the kernel driver and decodes the results (id-ctrl, id-ns, smart-log, error-log, get-log, get-feature, show-regs, list-subsys...). Some subcommands are destructive (format, sanitize, fw-commit).

Linux tool that records block-layer events (queue, dispatch, complete, split, merge) for a device; formatted by blkparse and summarized by btt. It sees requests above the NVMe driver, not QIDs or CIDs.

A named instrumentation point compiled into the kernel (e.g. nvme:nvme_setup_cmd, nvme:nvme_complete_rq) that can be enabled at run time with ftrace, trace-cmd, perf or bpftrace to record events with fields.
Linux command that prints the kernel's in-memory log ring buffer for the current boot, with monotonic timestamps by default; older messages are overwritten when the buffer fills.
Command that reads the systemd journal; -k selects kernel messages, -b -1 a previous boot (if the journal is persistent), -o short-monotonic shows kernel monotonic timestamps.
A PCIe capability of downstream ports that, on configured uncorrectable errors, disables the link below the port to contain the error until software recovers it; Linux logs 'DPC: containment event'.

Open-source machine emulator and virtualizer; its NVMe device model ('-device nvme', 'nvme-ns', 'nvme-subsys') provides a software NVMe controller backed by an image file, the course's safe practice target.

A set of user-space libraries and tools including a polled-mode NVMe driver; using it unbinds the device from the kernel nvme driver (vfio-pci/UIO), which is a caution-level operation on real hardware.
